questions.explanation: In inverted conditionals 'if' is dropped: 'Had I known'.
questions.q: ___ I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.

questions.explanation: 'Were I to...' introduces a hypothetical future, so the main clause uses 'would'.
questions.q: Were I to accept the job, I ___ relocate to Singapore.

questions.explanation: Invert 'If you had asked me' by dropping 'if' and fronting 'Had'.
options: Had you asked me, I had helped you.
If you had asked me, I would helped you.
Had you asked me, I would have helped you.
Were you had asked me, I would have helped you.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Should you have...' is the inverted form of a first conditional.
questions.q: Should you ___ any further questions, don't hesitate to contact us.

questions.explanation: 'Were it not for' takes a 'would have' result for a past hypothetical.
questions.q: Were it not for your support, the project ___ failed.

questions.explanation: 'Had + past participle' pairs with 'would have + past participle' for past hypotheticals.
questions.q: Had the manager not intervened, the negotiations ___ collapsed.

questions.explanation: 'Were + subject + to' inverts a hypothetical future condition.
questions.q: ___ you to change your mind, the offer will still stand.

questions.explanation: Invert 'If I had been rich' by dropping 'if' and fronting 'Had'.
options: Had I been rich, I would have traveled the world.
If I had been rich, I would travel the world.
Had I been rich, I would traveled the world.
Were I been rich, I would have traveled the world.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: The fixed inverted phrase is 'Were I in your/his position' (= If I were in...).
questions.q: Were I ___ his position, I'd resign immediately.

questions.explanation: This is an inverted mixed conditional: past condition, present result — 'would be'.
questions.q: Had they invested earlier, they ___ millionaires now.

questions.explanation: Inversion and 'if' never combine — delete 'if'.
options: Had she studied harder, she'd have passed.
Were he to call, tell him I'm out.
Should you see Anna, give her my regards.
Had if the train been late, we would have missed the flight.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'Had it not been for...' = 'If it had not been for...'.
questions.q: ___ not been for the rain, the match would have continued.

questions.explanation: 'Should + infinitive' introduces a possible future, so the result uses 'will'.
questions.q: Should the talks break down, the company ___ for bankruptcy.

questions.explanation: 'Were the data...' is hypothetical, so the result uses 'would be'.
questions.q: Were the data more reliable, the conclusion ___ different.

questions.explanation: After inverted 'Should', use the bare infinitive.
options: Should you needed help, call me.
Should you will need help, call me.
Should you would need help, call me.
Should you need help, call me.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Had + past participle' pairs with 'would have + past participle' for past regrets.
questions.q: Had we realized the risks, we ___ never signed the contract.

questions.explanation: 'Were + subject + to-infinitive' inverts a hypothetical future condition.
questions.q: ___ she to win the lottery, she wouldn't quit her job.

questions.explanation: A past hypothetical result needs 'would have'.
questions.q: Had the results been published sooner, the debate ___ taken a different turn.

questions.explanation: Invert 'If I were you' to 'Were I you'; a hypothetical present result uses 'would'.
options: Was I you, I would accept the offer.
Were I you, I will accept the offer.
Were I you, I would have accepted the offer.
Were I you, I would accept the offer.
questions.q: Choose the correct inverted conditional.

questions.explanation: A past hypothetical uses inverted 'Had + past participle'.
questions.q: ___ the alarm not sounded, no one would have evacuated.

topic: Conditionals: inversion (Had I known..., Were I to...)
